findings.highlight: I can see the start of the stairs about ten meters directly above me
findings.evidenceJa: 正面のシンボルの真上高さにして十メートルほどの位置に、降りてきた階段の入り口が見えた
findings.governingReading: The stair entrance is visible about ten meters up, directly above the symbol before him.
findings.explanation: The entrance is relocated from above the facing symbol to above Shirou.

findings.highlight: Beyond it, an entrance to darkness is open
findings.evidenceJa: その正反対の壁に、黒い闇が[ruby text=あ]穿いている
findings.governingReading: In the wall exactly opposite it, black darkness gapes / pierces through.
findings.explanation: Precise opposition and the punctured-wall image become a generic entrance beyond the symbol.

findings.highlight: the feeling that my leg would rot every time I step in it
findings.evidenceJa: 歩くたびに、踝まで腐っていくような感覚
findings.governingReading: With every step, it feels as though the rot reaches up to his ankles.
findings.explanation: A present, spatially bounded sensation becomes a hypothetical rotting leg.

findings.highlight: an awful stench
findings.evidenceJa: 強い刺激臭
findings.governingReading: a strong, irritating odor
findings.explanation: A specific pungent chemical quality becomes generic foulness.

findings.highlight: It’s not the smell of meat
findings.evidenceJa: 生臭い匂いではない
findings.governingReading: It is not a raw, bloody/fishy reek.
findings.explanation: The sensory category is mistranslated as meat.

findings.highlight: The smell of medicine fills this room
findings.evidenceJa: 酔ってしまうほどの薬品の匂いが、この部屋には泥のように沈殿している
findings.governingReading: A chemical smell strong enough to intoxicate has settled in the room like mud.
findings.explanation: The intoxication, sediment, and mud simile disappear.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel any chills or pressures anymore
findings.evidenceJa: 緊張も悪寒も、とっくに感じなくなっている
findings.governingReading: He no longer feels tension or chills.
findings.explanation: Psychological tension is replaced by unspecified pressure.

findings.highlight: My heart beats like it’s expanding to twice its size
findings.evidenceJa: 心臓は休みなく拡縮を繰り返し
findings.governingReading: His heart endlessly repeats contraction and expansion.
findings.explanation: The English adds a doubling in size absent from the source.

findings.highlight: my hands are vermiculating like they’re going to crumble into pieces
findings.evidenceJa: 手足の感覚は粉々に砕けていきそうなほど[ruby text=ぜんどう char=2]蠕動している
findings.governingReading: Sensation in his hands and feet writhes/peristalses as if about to shatter.
findings.explanation: The feet and sensory subject disappear, and a malformed rare verb obscures the bodily image.

findings.highlight: There are corpses. There are corpses. There are corpses. There are corpses. There are corpses all around me.
findings.evidenceJa: 死が、並んでいる
findings.governingReading: Death is lined up.
findings.explanation: The English inserts repeated corpse lines and later detailed feeding imagery absent from the active Japanese page.

findings.highlight: That’s the cause of the dripping sound. The water is dripping into the corpses’ mouths.
findings.evidenceJa: たちこめる死臭を、幾重もの薬香が塗り潰す
findings.governingReading: Layer upon layer of medicinal fragrance paints over the pervasive odor of death.
findings.explanation: The medicinal masking image is followed by invented water-feeding, swollen lips, and decomposing jaws.

findings.highlight: I tell myself that this isn’t happening. I don’t want to think that such a thing can happen
findings.evidenceJa: 嘘だ、と思った。こんなものは嘘なのだと思いたかった
findings.governingReading: He thought it was a lie; he wanted to believe such a thing was a lie.
findings.explanation: The repeated wish to deny reality becomes denial of occurrence and then reluctance to imagine possibility.

findings.highlight: I remember a news story I heard somewhere. It was a story about a whale.
findings.evidenceJa: どうして生きているのか
findings.governingReading: Why are they alive?
findings.explanation: A long whale-stomach survival anecdote absent from the active Japanese is inserted before the question.

findings.highlight: No limbs. Those that have had them cut off. Those that have had the ends decomposed, leaving only the bone.
findings.evidenceJa: そのどれもが、あまりにも、形を止めていない
findings.governingReading: None retains anything approaching its former shape.
findings.explanation: The English inserts a separate catalog of amputations and exposed bone beyond this source page.

findings.highlight: I don’t even need to know why
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=ワケ o2o=1]理由を[ruby text=ミ]調るまでもない
findings.governingReading: There is no need to inspect the reason / mechanism.
findings.explanation: The written words and ruby readings that combine reason with inspection disappear.

findings.highlight: the corpses are stuck to the coffin
findings.evidenceJa: 死体は棺に溶接され
findings.governingReading: The bodies are welded to the coffin.
findings.explanation: A violent mechanical attachment becomes generic adhesion.

findings.highlight: The coffin is sucking up magical energy… no, something close to the soul
findings.evidenceJa: 魔力、いや魂に近いものを棺は搾取している
findings.governingReading: The coffin exploits/extracts magical energy—no, something close to the soul.
findings.explanation: Deliberate exploitation is reduced to the already-stated physical suction.

findings.highlight: Their throats have already decayed
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らの喉はとっくに退化し
findings.governingReading: Their throats have long since atrophied.
findings.explanation: Loss of function through atrophy becomes decomposition.

findings.highlight: It has already become just an organ to keep them alive
findings.evidenceJa: 生きながらえるだけの気管になり下がっている
findings.governingReading: It has been reduced to an airway fit only to prolong survival.
findings.explanation: The concrete airway and degrading register are generalized.

findings.highlight: In an almost inaudible voice, they scream with all their might
findings.evidenceJa: 蚊の泣くような声で、精一杯の絶叫をあげ続ける
findings.governingReading: In voices like mosquitoes crying, they continue their utmost screams.
findings.explanation: The acoustic simile and continuous death-cry quality disappear.

findings.highlight: An eye drops off as it turns its neck towards me. But stillit stares directly at me.
findings.evidenceJa: 頭から、滑ったモノがこぼれ落ちる
findings.governingReading: Something slick spills from the head as it turns toward him.
findings.explanation: The English specifies an eye and adds a stare absent from the active Japanese, then repeats the source action.

findings.highlight: Where am I? And asks me that question.
findings.evidenceJa: ここは　どこ
findings.governingReading: It asks him, “Where is this?”
findings.explanation: The question and reporting clause are split into malformed English.

findings.highlight: He was like that before he realized it?
findings.evidenceJa: あの子は、気が付いたらああだったのか
findings.governingReading: Was that child already like this when he came to?
findings.explanation: The timing relation between awakening and discovering the condition is reversed.

findings.highlight: His limbs are already gone, sucked Sucked by that coffin, rotting away from the ends, unable to move
findings.evidenceJa: あんな棺に収納され、動く事もできず末端から腐って
findings.governingReading: Stored in that coffin, unable to move, rotting from the extremities.
findings.explanation: Missing limbs, suction, duplicated debris, and altered syntax are inserted.

findings.highlight: (As if knowing me) …Staring at me?
findings.evidenceJa: （俺が知っているかのように）
findings.governingReading: Why do they all stare as if they know him—as if he knows them?
findings.explanation: The parenthetical reversal from their recognition to his recognition disappears.

findings.highlight: Is it some coincidence, or do the sacrifices have to meet this condition?
findings.evidenceJa: ただの偶然なのか、それが共通項なのか、生け贄はそうでなくてはならないのか
findings.governingReading: Is it coincidence, a shared trait, or a requirement for the sacrifices?
findings.explanation: A three-way question becomes two alternatives.

findings.highlight: I’m tapped on the shoulder
findings.evidenceJa: バン、と両肩を叩かれた
findings.governingReading: Both shoulders are struck with a bang.
findings.explanation: The number, force, and sound of Kotomine’s mock-friendly greeting disappear.

findings.highlight: a devil I must not meet more than anything else in this place
findings.evidenceJa: 今、最も出会ってはいけない悪魔
findings.governingReading: the devil he must least of all encounter now
findings.explanation: The English is malformed and weakens the immediate superlative threat.

findings.highlight: I’m frightened
findings.evidenceJa: それが、喩えようもなく恐ろしかった
findings.governingReading: That was terrifying beyond comparison.
findings.explanation: The degree and causal emphasis collapse into a generic emotion.

findings.highlight: Is this spectacle really so outrageous?
findings.evidenceJa: それほどこの光景は奇怪かね
findings.governingReading: Is this spectacle so bizarre?
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s clinical appraisal becomes moral outrage.

findings.highlight: The priest says inhuman things in a cheerful voice
findings.evidenceJa: 神父は親しげな声で、人間味のない言葉を口にした
findings.governingReading: The priest speaks inhuman words in a friendly, familiar voice.
findings.explanation: The cultivated false intimacy is replaced by cheerfulness.

findings.highlight: you and these corpses are fellow mates
findings.evidenceJa: この死体たちとおまえは仲間だった
findings.governingReading: You and these bodies were comrades / fellows.
findings.explanation: The key survivor-group relation is rendered with malformed redundant English.

findings.highlight: I avoided thinking about it
findings.evidenceJa: 知ることも避けていた
findings.governingReading: He had also avoided finding out.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s deliberate avoidance of knowledge becomes avoidance of thought.

findings.highlight: you survive
findings.evidenceJa: おまえだけが和を乱して生きのびた
findings.governingReading: You alone disrupted the common order by surviving.
findings.explanation: Kotomine’s accusation that Shirou’s survival breaks the group’s equality disappears.

findings.highlight: extract the same amount of soul
findings.evidenceJa: 濃い[ruby text=たましい char=2]苦痛の摘出
findings.governingReading: extract the same concentrated pain, read as “soul.”
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the ruby reading and erases the written claim that suffering itself is extracted.

findings.highlight: I lack the things people need to move
findings.evidenceJa: 人間として活動するのに、必要なモノが欠けている
findings.governingReading: He lacks what is necessary to function as a human being.
findings.explanation: Loss of human functioning is narrowed to inability to move.

findings.highlight: this white, burning pain
findings.evidenceJa: 真っ白い、黒こげになりそうな痛み
findings.governingReading: pain that is pure white yet feels about to char him black
findings.explanation: The white/blackened sensory paradox loses its endpoint.

findings.highlight: It should be about half an hour
findings.evidenceJa: およそ半時というところか
findings.governingReading: approximately half a toki—about one hour
findings.explanation: The historical time unit is halved.

findings.highlight: Pain finally overcomes my brain
findings.evidenceJa: 痛みはついに脳の許容量を超え
findings.governingReading: The pain finally exceeds his brain’s capacity.
findings.explanation: A capacity threshold becomes the brain itself as an opponent.

findings.highlight: if I faint here, I also know that I’ll die
findings.evidenceJa: ここで意識を失えば、もう目覚める事はない
findings.governingReading: If he loses consciousness here, he knows he will never wake again.
findings.explanation: The fatal implication is promoted into a directly stated fact.

findings.highlight: I can’t just disappear here
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=オレ char=4]衛宮士郎は、こんなところで、消える訳にはいかない筈だ
findings.governingReading: Emiya Shirou—read “I”—cannot be allowed to disappear here.
findings.explanation: The written full identity and first-person ruby anchoring his resolve disappear.
